title: The agent that interrupted itself
blurb: Barge-in raced the TTS offset and the draft replayed audio on retry.
prompt: A user interrupted the agent and it kept talking to the end of the sentence; a reconnect later replayed the first two sentences of audio, and the client was billed for both. The model-generated draft updates barge-in state in two commands and restarts TTS from offset zero. Review it, fix it, and prove interruption is atomic and audio never replays.
aiNote: The draft writes the speaker change and the TTS offset as separate commands, so a barge-in can land between them and the agent speaks over the user, and its TTS retry restarts the stream at the beginning, re-billing and re-playing delivered audio.
testIdea: Race a barge-in with an audio frame and assert the agent's stream is truncated at the current token; fail TTS mid-response and assert the retry resumes at the delivered offset or errors without replaying audio.
followUps: What is the right behavior when ASR confidence is low for the whole turn?
How would you cap a session's cost without cutting off a long legitimate answer?
What redaction happens before a transcript is stored?
